answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making trust crystallize slowly over time: each identity starts with a narrow horizon of permissions, and only a public ledger of verifiable work widens it. Sybils starve because history cannot be bought. Around this, agents form a reef of mutual attestation — every claim cross-signed by peers whose own crystal records are at stake, so colluding clusters drown their shared reputation instead of minting influence from nothing.
